newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Canada discuss aluminium statistical body.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Canada discuss aluminium statistical body.

text.p: Russian and Canadian aluminium officials met on Friday to discuss setting up a statistical body to exchange production information -- and output curbs were not mentioned, a Canadian diplomat said.

The diplomat, who asked not to be identified, said officials discussed setting up the International Statistical Working Group on Aluminium, in which aluminium producers would exchange and publish information on how they gather statistics.
"There's not even a founding document for this group," said the source, who said participants had no plans for face-to-face meeting. "We're just writing statistics and faxing them."
He said the group was Canada's idea.

He reiterated Canadian officials' comments that producers had not intended and did not intend to discuss a new output cutting deal similar to the March 1994 two-year Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between producing countries Russia, Canada, Australia, Norway, the European Union and the United States.

Russian Kontsern Alyuminiy producers' group officials said earlier this month that Russia was considering not using capacity idled under the old MOU and that others might agree to do the same to boost flagging world prices.

The talk, much of its based on vague market rumours, evoked memories of the MOU, which was criticised by some for artificially shaping the market. "I think that they (the Russians) went fishing," said one source.
When asked earlier if any output curbs were in the works, a Canadian official said , "No -- do you hear me? No. We are not, repeat not, repeat not, discussing a new MOU."
